messages.content: Originalism advocates for interpreting the Second Amendment based on its original public understanding at the time of its ratification, arguing that the Founders intended a specific, limited set of rights. Proponents emphasize limiting judicial discretion to the historical meaning of the text. Conversely, living constitutionalists argue that the Amendment's meaning must evolve with contemporary societal understandings and technology. They contend that a static interpretation cannot adequately address modern challenges to armed self-defense.
